title: [Platform system health] ASIC key is not handled properly in system health daemon
author: aravindmani-1
body:
**Description**
The ASIC table key used in system health is “TEMPERATURE_INFO|ASIC”. 
https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/blob/a64994ec298bc8cae8f8b03216d6c4e1ed27586e/src/system-health/health_checker/hardware_checker.py#L11

In Dell platforms, we don’t have this key.
    root@sonic:/# redis-cli -n  6  hgetall  "TEMPERATURE_INFO|ASIC"
    (empty array)
    root@sonic:~#

The available list of keys for Dell S6100 are 
root@sonic:~# redis-cli -n 6 keys "*TEMPERATURE_INFO*"
1) "TEMPERATURE_INFO|ASIC On-board Rear"
2) "TEMPERATURE_INFO|CPU Core 1"
3) "TEMPERATURE_INFO|CPU Core 2"
4) "TEMPERATURE_INFO|Front GE board"
5) "TEMPERATURE_INFO|CPU On-board"
6) "TEMPERATURE_INFO|ASIC On-board Front"
7) "TEMPERATURE_INFO|System Front"
8) "TEMPERATURE_INFO|CPU Core 3"
9) "TEMPERATURE_INFO|Front SFP+ board"
10) "TEMPERATURE_INFO|CPU Core 0"
root@sonic:~#


If we change the system health code to retrieve one of the keys mentioned(ASIC on-board Rear /ASIC on-board Front”), the error was not seen.
root@sonic:~# show system-health summary              
  Services:
    Status: OK
  Hardware:
    Status: OK


**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Load master image and create a system health json file for Dell S6100 platform.
2. Check show system-health summary in Dell S6100

**Describe the results you received:**
In some Dell platforms, we’ve only one ASIC sensor(ASIC On-board) alone.
Currently, ASIC Temperature error will be logged when executing system health CLI if this issue is not fixed.
root@sonic:~# show system-health summary
  Services:
    Status: OK
  Hardware:
    Status: Not OK
    Reasons: Failed to get ASIC temperature


**Describe the results you expected:**
Status was set to OK when ASIC key(ASIC on-board Front/Rear is used).

comments.author: sujinmkang
comments.body:
@keboliu, @Junchao-Mellanox: Can you please comment on this?
And also I have one question in addition to this issue, why does the system health daemon check only the ASIC temperature not other components' temperature?

comments.author: Junchao-Mellanox
comments.body:
Hi @sujinmkang , 

1. Why we hard code "TEMPERATURE_INFO|ASIC" as the key of ASIC thermal object?  I remember I had some discussion with the community when review the HLD. It is not possible to get ASIC temperature among all thermal objects without knowing the ASIC key. So we got an agreement that, the thermal name for ASIC should be "ASIC" for all vendors and it is vendor's responsibility to align it. 
2. Why does the system health daemon check only the ASIC temperature not other components's temperature? I suppose the reason is that not all thermal object defines the "get_high_threshold" function. For example, not all SFP cables has the ability to get its temperature and temperature threshold. As SFP cables can be replaced and different cables have different thermal capability, it is hard to check such thermal object in system health. As ASIC   temperature is very/most critical to the switch, we only check its temperature in system health.

As there are multi ASIC support in SONiC now, maybe we need update this design a litter bit, what do you suggest?

comments.author: aravindmani-1
comments.body:
Hi @Junchao-Mellanox,

Regarding the first item, If there are multiple ASIC keys(ASIC on-board Front/Rear), we can not have the same ASIC key name.
How do you want to handle this?.

comments.author: sujinmkang
comments.body:
@Junchao-Mellanox  and @aravindmani-1 
To support multi-ASIC and multiple internal sensor in each ASIC, I want to re-define the DB schema as below.
The ASIC thermal monitoring hld (https://github.com/Azure/SONiC/blob/master/doc/asic_thermal_monitoring_hld.md) has defined multiple temperature sensor reading for each ASIC.
thermalctld uses the temperature values from the state db updated by the ASIC thermal monitoring polling module.
```
; Defines information for an ASIC thermal object
key                               =  "TEMPERATURE_INFO|ASIC {}"
; field                            = value
timestamp                    = STRING                         ; timestamp for the temperature fetched
high_threshold             = FLOAT                          ; temperature high threshold
critical_high_threshold = FLOAT                          ; temperature critical high threshold
low_threshold               = FLOAT                          ; temperature low threshold
critical_low_threshold   = FLOAT                          ; temperature critical low threshold
warning_status             = BOOLEAN                     ; temperature warning status
average_temperature    = FLOAT                          ; current average temperature value
maximum_temperature  = FLOAT                         ; maximum temperature value
temperature_0              = FLOAT                          ; ASIC internal sensor 0 temperature value
...
temperature_N              = FLOAT                          ; ASIC internal sensor N temperature value
```
Please share your comments if you have any other idea.

comments.author: aravindmani-1
comments.body: @sujinmkang I don't think ASIC on-board Front/Rear sensors will have internal temperature 0 to N sensors.

linkedPullRequests.author: aravindmani-1
linkedPullRequests.body:
**- Why I did it**
ASIC key used in system health daemon is not present in Dell platforms.
Fixes https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/issues/6343 
**- How I did it**
Got the thermal sensor list using 2.0 API and retrieved the ASIC keys.
**- How to verify it**
Check "show system-health summary/detail/monitor-list" 
**- Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)**


- [ ] 201811
- [ ] 201911
- [ ] 202006
- [ ] 202012

**- Description for the changelog**
Get the platform based ASIC keys used in thermal sensor list.
UT logs:
[system_health_UT.txt](https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/files/5867573/system_health_UT.txt)

comments.author: aravindmani-1
comments.body: @sujinmkang , @jleveque , @Junchao-Mellanox can you please review this PR?.

comments.author: Junchao-Mellanox
comments.body:
To me, there are two issues in this solution:

1. thermals belonging to chassis does not have to be a ASIC thermal, they can be CPU sensors and so on.  We probably should not treat it as "ASIC overheat"
2. There could be thermal which does not support getting threshold, in that case, we might need provide a way to ignore such thermal.

comments.author: aravindmani-1
Junchao-Mellanox
comments.body:
> @Junchao-Mellanox
> Currently, we consider ASIC temperature only in system health daemon.
> If ASIC is not present/mentioned in ignore devices in platform specific config file, it won't even execute the current solution.

chassis.get_all_thermals() may return a list of thermal objects. And these thermal objects may or may not have threshold available, it is not so good to ignore them all by adding "asic" to the ignore devices.

comments.author: aravindmani-1
comments.body: @Junchao-Mellanox I agree that some thermal sensors may not have threshold value but here, we retrieve only the ASIC keys from the thermal sensors list and get the threshold for the respective ASIC sensor. Correct me if i understood anything.
